intro.text: TOW watches topics on torrent sites. When a topic page gets a new version, TOW hands it to your torrent client (qBittorrent, Transmission or Deluge) and tells the connected messengers. TOW itself downloads nothing and does not move files — the client does that.

s1.title: 1. Sections
s1.home: Home — the topics TOW watches: link, name, folder in the torrent client.
s1.sites: Sites — where the topics come from (rutor, kinozal…). A site can have several mirror addresses: if one does not answer, TOW takes the next.
s1.settings: Settings — torrent clients, notifications, how often to check, access from other devices, the service and backups.
s1.log: Log (the list icon in the header) — recent events. Passwords never get there. The log does not grow forever: {n} files of {size} each are kept.

s2.title: 2. How to add a topic
s2.step2: You can keep the suggested name and folder. The folder is where the torrent client saves the files.
s2.step3: TOW checks the topic at once and, if the client is reachable, hands it to the client; you get the message “… — added to the torrent client”.
s2.dot: The dot in a row is the result of the last check: green — all fine, blue — something new found, yellow — the site is temporarily unavailable (TOW will try again), red — your help is needed (the reason is under the name; open the row — click or tap it, or press Enter — for the full text), grey — not checked yet.
s2.icon: The site icon shows the site alone: a torrent client or folder error does not color it.
s2.step1: Home → + → paste the link to the topic page on the site.

s3.title: 3. How to add a site
s3.step2: The easiest way is to paste a link to any topic on that site — the fields fill in by themselves.
s3.step3: If the file cannot be downloaded without signing in, enter the site's login and password. They are stored encrypted.
s3.step4: The address you click in the site's row becomes the main one; the globe icon opens it.
s3.note: If a site address does not answer three times in a row, TOW skips it for an hour and tries the others; the “Check” button in the site's row ends this pause. When a site says “download limit for today”, TOW leaves it alone until tomorrow.

s4.title: 4. Notifications
s4.text: Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp and ntfy are in Settings → Notifications. Each has “How to connect” steps and a “Check” button. Every message goes to all connected messengers. If a messenger is unavailable, the message waits and goes out later by itself. The bell in the header: green — messages get through, red — some messenger did not accept a message, grey — nothing is connected.

s5.title: 5. Checks and the clock in the header
s5.text: Topics are checked automatically every {interval} (change it in Settings → Checks). The clock in the header shows the time until the next check. Every 10 minutes the watchdog makes sure TOW is running: if TOW has stopped or hangs, it starts it again and reports the cause.

s6.title: 6. Backups
s6.night: Nightly backups are made automatically every night; if a backup fails, you get a message. You can choose the folder, including another drive or a network folder.
s6.create: Create a backup — a backup “just in case” before important changes. Restore first checks the backup and saves the current state.
s6.note: A backup holds the settings, topics, history and encrypted passwords. Downloaded files and the torrent client itself are not in it. The address, port and access from other devices stay as they are when you restore.
s6.file: TOW file (.towx) — a full encrypted copy of this TOW. Restoring it needs the same encryption key (keys/master.key): on another computer, put that key there first — it is not in the file, so keep it separately, for example on a USB stick. To move TOW to an install with a different key, use tow export and tow import in a terminal: their file is protected by a passphrase instead.

s7.title: 7. Access from a phone or laptop
s7.text: On this computer TOW opens without a password. From other devices — only with a password (Settings → Network access); a device stays signed in for 90 days. Access and the password can only be changed on this computer.

s8.title: 8. Where the data is
s8.config: — settings and the list of sites (without passwords).
s8.secrets: — encrypted passwords and tokens. The encryption key is kept apart from the data.
s8.note: An empty password field in a form means “keep as is”; saved passwords are never shown.

history.title: History
history.note: Shows up to 300 latest events from the log (5 files of 5 MiB).
history.no_events: No events yet. Checks, downloads and changes appear here.

add.name: Name
add.selection_hint: Leave it empty for “all files”. If nothing matches, or the match is unclear, nothing is started.
add.check_hint: A normal check can add a torrent to the torrent client. TOW itself does not download, copy or move files.
add.add_site: Add this site on the Sites page first
add.title: Add a topic
add.checking_note: TOW is checking the topic on the site and handing it to the torrent client — this can take up to a minute. The page opens by itself when it is done.

auth.title: Sign-in needed

telegram.step_bot: Send @BotFather the command /newbot and choose a name — it will send you the bot token.
telegram.step_start: Open your bot and press “Start” (or send it anything).
telegram.step_id: Find out your ID: message @userinfobot — it replies with a number.
telegram.step_save: Paste the token and ID below, press “Save”, then “Check”.
telegram.note: Several recipients are fine: IDs separated by commas (for a group, its ID with a minus sign).
telegram.token_error: a token looks like 123456789:AA… — copy the whole token from @BotFather

discord.step_channel: In Discord, open the channel → ⚙ “Edit Channel” → “Integrations” → “Webhooks”.
discord.step_new: Press “New Webhook”; you may name it TOW.
discord.step_save: Paste the address below, press “Save”, then “Check”.
discord.note: The webhook address is a key to the channel: TOW keeps it encrypted and never shows it to anyone.

whatsapp.step_save: Enter your WhatsApp number and this apikey below, press “Save”, then “Check”.
whatsapp.note: Messages go through the free CallMeBot service, not the official WhatsApp API: it needs no business account, but it dislikes frequent messages — TOW groups them anyway.
whatsapp.phone_error: the number in international format, for example +15551234567

access.q: access lan local network password authentication
access.title: Network access
access.intro: On this computer TOW opens without a password. From other devices — a phone, a laptop, through Tailscale — only with a password; a device stays signed in for 90 days, even after TOW restarts. Changing the password signs TOW out on every device.
access.allow: Open TOW from other devices (with a password)
access.password_hint: At least 8 characters. Easy to remember: three or four words joined with hyphens.
access.local_only: Access from other devices is switched on or off only on the computer running TOW — so nobody on the network can lock you out of TOW.
access.keep_password: Leave empty to keep the password and change only the reminder
access.hint_help: Shown on the sign-in page under “Forgot your password?”. Anyone on your network who opens that page can read it — never write the password itself.
access.reset_here: Forgot the password? On this computer a new one is set without the old one. Other devices then sign in again.
access.reset_elsewhere: From another device the current password is needed. Forgot it? Set a new one on the computer running TOW. Other devices then sign in again; this one stays signed in.
access.sign_out_hint: Every device signed in over the network has to enter the password again; the password stays the same. Use it after signing in on someone else's phone or computer.
access.need_password_first: Set a password above first: without it no other device can sign in.
access.no_password: No password set — TOW cannot be opened from other devices right now. Set a password below.

service.title: TOW service
service.restart_confirm: Restart TOW? The page may be unavailable for a few seconds.
service.restart_note: The page will be unavailable for a few seconds.
service.watchdog: The watchdog checks the schedule and reports downtime and its cause to connected messengers. The running supervisor restarts the web server after a failure; the watchdog does not restart TOW itself.
service.doctor_note: — connection to the torrent client, the sites and the running service.
service.no_restarts: TOW has not been restarted from here yet.
service.mode_supervisor: TOW runs as one process: the web page, scheduled checks, night copies and the watchdog.
service.autostart_hint_any: Start TOW when you sign in to this computer. The change takes effect at once.
service.without_login_hint: TOW starts with the computer, before anyone signs in. Windows may ask for administrator rights, and network folders are then not reachable; on Linux it needs one command, which TOW shows.

backups.title: Backups
backups.night_hint: Every night at 03:30 (or when the computer is turned on, if it was off) TOW copies its settings, history and encrypted passwords. The last 14 are kept. If a backup fails or there has been none for more than a day and a half, you get a message.
backups.night_restore_confirm: Restore the settings and history from the nightly backup of {at}? TOW saves its current state separately first.
backups.folders_hint: You can choose another drive or a network folder (\\server\folder — then it is reachable at night too). “Check” tries to write a file.
backups.list_error: The list of backups is not available right now.
backups.manual_restore_confirm: Restore the settings and history from this backup? TOW saves its current state automatically before replacing it.
backups.manual_note: Before restoring, TOW checks the backup and saves its current state. The network settings stay as they are now. The last 10 backups are kept.
backups.file_intro: A full encrypted copy to keep or to move TOW to another computer.
backups.file_restore_confirm: Restore TOW from this file? The current state is saved automatically before it is replaced.
backups.file_note: Restoring always checks the file again and makes a safety copy first. More.

setup.heading: Welcome to TOW
setup.intro: On this computer TOW opens without a password. To open it from a phone or a laptop, set a password — now, or later in Settings → Network access.
setup.reset_note: Forgot it later? A new password is set on this computer without the old one.

setup.what: TOW watches topics on torrent sites. When a topic gets a new version, TOW hands it to your torrent client (qBittorrent, Transmission or Deluge) and can tell you about it in a messenger. TOW itself downloads nothing and does not move files.
setup.step_client: Connect your torrent client: Settings → Torrent clients.
setup.step_notify: Optional: connect a messenger for notifications: Settings → Notifications.
setup.step_topic: On Home, press + and paste the link to a topic page. A site TOW does not know yet is added on the Sites page.
setup.after_hint: Home shows these steps until the first topic is added.

backup.copy_missing: ; not in the copy because they do not exist yet: {names}

settings.client_added: {title} added — fill in the connection below and press “Save”
settings.default_client: main client chosen: TOW adds new torrents to it
settings.access_local_only: access and password can be changed only on the PC running TOW
settings.restart_started: restart started; check the service health
settings.restore_failed: restore did not run; current data is kept
settings.file_ok: the file is fine; it can be restored
settings.restored_file: restored from the file; LAN access kept
settings.rollback_critical: critical rollback error; data may have changed
settings.file_invalid: the file did not pass the check; data unchanged
settings.safety_point_failed: the file is fine; could not create a safety point; data unchanged
settings.file_unreadable: could not read the file; data unchanged
settings.password_again: address or login changed — enter the client password again
settings.notifier_private_host: the server must be an internet address: TOW does not send to this PC or the home network (for your own server at home: allow_private_notifier_hosts: true in config.yaml)
settings.ping_login: the client did not accept the login or password
settings.ping_unreachable: the client does not answer at this address and port, or its web interface is off

sites.login_host_not_mirror: the login address must be one of the mirrors
sites.password_again: new login address — enter the site password again
sites.not_saved: the site change was not saved; everything is as it was
sites.regex_missing: Topic link pattern: fill it in, or paste a topic link to fill in the form
sites.exists: A site named “{name}” already exists — open its row below to change it

doctor.client_down: the torrent client does not answer

password.saved: password saved; other devices sign in again
password.store_unavailable: the password was not changed: the secrets store is unavailable
password.signed_out: every other device has been signed out; they need the password to come back

nnmclub.browser_login: Sign in to NNMClub and pass Turnstile in the window that opened

store.state_newer: state.json was written by a newer TOW (data version {found}; this TOW knows {known}). Update TOW or restore a backup made by this version; nothing was changed.
store.state_bad_version: state.json has a data version this TOW cannot read ({found}); nothing was changed. Restore it from a restore point or a backup.
store.no_master_key: The master key is missing, so the saved passwords and tokens cannot be opened. Put the key file back as keys/master.key in the install (or point TOW_MASTER_KEY_FILE at it), or bring it in with: tow keys adopt --from FILE. On a new install without saved secrets, run: tow keys ensure
store.key_path_outside_data: A relative TOW_MASTER_KEY_FILE path must stay inside the TOW data folder. Use an absolute path for an external key file.

not_found.title: Page not found
not_found.heading: This page does not exist
not_found.text: The address may be old or mistyped. Everything TOW has is reachable from the header.
